p.src: Now Gao Shun led Zhang Liao in an attack on Lord Guan's camp, while Lü Bu himself attacked Zhang Fei's. Guan and Zhang each rode out to meet them, and Xuande led troops to support both wings. Lü Bu divided his forces and struck from the rear. Both Guan's and Zhang's armies collapsed, and Xuande fled back to Pei with several dozen horsemen. Lü Bu pursued him, and Xuande urgently called to the soldiers atop the walls to lower the drawbridge. Lü Bu arrived close behind him. The men on the walls wished to loose their arrows, but feared they might hit Xuande. Seizing the moment, Lü Bu charged through the gate. Its defenders could not withstand him and scattered in every direction. Lü Bu summoned his troops into the city. Seeing how desperate matters had become, Xuande had no time to return home. He could only abandon his wife and children, ride through the city and out of the west gate, and flee alone on horseback.

p.src: Lü Bu then reached Xuande's residence, where Mi Zhu came out to meet him and said, “I have heard that a true man does no harm to another man's wife and children. The one now contending with you for the realm is Lord Cao alone. Xuande has always remembered your kindness in shooting the halberd at the camp gate and would never dare betray you. He has gone over to Lord Cao now only because he had no other choice. I beg you to show him mercy.” Lü Bu said, “Xuande and I are old friends. How could I bear to harm his wife and children?” He thereupon ordered Mi Zhu to escort Xuande's family to Xuzhou and settle them there. Lü Bu himself led his army toward the borders of Yanzhou in Shandong, leaving Gao Shun and Zhang Liao to defend Xiaopei. By this time Sun Qian had already escaped from the city. Guan and Zhang had each rallied some troops and taken up positions in the hills.

p.src: Meanwhile Xuande was fleeing alone on horseback when a man caught up from behind. Looking back, he saw that it was Sun Qian. Xuande said, “I do not know whether my two brothers are alive or dead, and my wife and children are lost. What am I to do?” Sun Qian said, “For now, we had best seek refuge with Cao Cao and then devise our future course.” Xuande followed his advice and took byroads toward the capital, Xu. They ran out of provisions on the way and sometimes went into villages to beg for food. Yet wherever they went, as soon as people heard that he was Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, they vied with one another to offer food and drink. One day they sought lodging at a house. A young man of the household came out and bowed; when asked his name, he proved to be a hunter named Liu An.

p.src: When Liu An learned that the Governor of Yuzhou had arrived, he wished to find game to serve him, but could procure none at such short notice; so he killed his wife and served her flesh as food. Xuande asked, “What meat is this?” Liu An replied, “It is wolf meat.” Xuande suspected nothing and ate his fill; when night fell, he lodged there. At dawn, as he was about to depart, he went to the rear courtyard to fetch his horse and suddenly saw a woman lying slain by the kitchen, all the flesh cut from her arms. Xuande asked in horror and only then learned that the flesh he had eaten the night before was that of Liu An's wife. Xuande was overcome with grief. Shedding tears, he mounted his horse. Liu An told Xuande, “I had wished to follow you, my lord, but my aged mother is still at home, so I dare not travel far.”

p.src: Xuande thanked him and took his leave, following the road out past Liangcheng. Suddenly he saw clouds of dust blotting out the sun as a great body of troops approached. Knowing them to be Cao Cao's forces, Xuande and Sun Qian went straight to the commander's banner and met Cao Cao. Xuande related in full how he had lost Pei, become separated from his two brothers, and left his wife and children trapped behind. Cao Cao too shed tears at the tale. When Xuande also told how Liu An had killed his wife to feed him, Cao Cao ordered Sun Qian to take Liu An a reward of one hundred taels of gold.

p.src: When the army reached Jibei, Xiahou Yuan and the others welcomed Cao Cao into camp and reported in detail that his elder brother Xiahou Dun had lost an eye and was still bedridden, not yet recovered. Cao Cao visited him at his bedside and ordered him to return first to the capital, Xu, to recuperate; at the same time, he sent men to discover Lü Bu's present whereabouts. The scouts returned and reported, “Lü Bu has allied himself with Chen Gong and Zang Ba and the bandits of Mount Tai, and together they are attacking the various commanderies of Yanzhou.” Cao Cao at once ordered Cao Ren to lead three thousand troops against Pei. Cao Cao himself took command of the main army and went with Xuande to do battle with Lü Bu. Advancing into Shandong, they neared Xiao Pass and encountered the Mount Tai outlaws Sun Guan, Wu Dun, Yin Li, and Chang Xi, who barred the road with more than thirty thousand troops. Cao Cao ordered Xu Chu to meet them in battle, and all four commanders rode out together. Xu Chu fought with desperate valor. Unable to withstand him, the four commanders were each put to flight. Cao Cao pressed the advantage and pursued them as far as Xiao Pass, where a scout sped off to report to Lü Bu.

p.src: By then Lü Bu had returned to Xuzhou. Intending to go with Chen Deng to relieve Xiaopei, he ordered Chen Gui to defend Xuzhou. As Chen Deng was about to depart, Chen Gui said to him, “Lord Cao once said that all affairs in the east were entrusted to you. Now Lü Bu is on the verge of defeat; this is your chance to act against him.” Chen Deng replied, “I shall attend to matters outside myself; if Lü Bu returns defeated, Father, invite Mi Zhu to help defend the city and do not let Lü Bu enter. I have my own plan for escaping.” Chen Gui said, “His wife and children are here, and he has many trusted adherents within the city. What can be done about them?” Chen Deng replied, “I have a plan for that as well.” He then went in to see Lü Bu and said, “Xuzhou is exposed to enemies on every side, and Cao Cao will surely attack it in force. We must first prepare a line of retreat. The money and provisions should be moved to Xiapi. If Xuzhou is besieged, supplies from Xiapi can come to its aid. Why do you not make plans at once, my lord?” Lü Bu said, “Yuanlong's counsel is excellent. I shall move my wife and children there as well.” He therefore ordered Song Xian and Wei Xu to escort his family, money, and provisions to Xiapi and station them there; meanwhile, he personally led troops with Chen Deng to the relief of Xiao Pass. Halfway there, Chen Deng said, “Allow me to go ahead to the pass and learn the true strength of Cao Cao's forces; then, my lord, you may advance.”

p.src: Lü Bu consented, and Chen Deng went ahead to the pass. Chen Gong and the others received him. Chen Deng said, “The Marquis of Wen is deeply angered that you refuse to advance and is coming to punish you.” Chen Gong said, “Cao Cao's forces are now too powerful to be taken lightly. Our best course is to hold the pass securely while you urge our lord to defend Pei with all his strength.” Chen Deng murmured his agreement. That evening he climbed the pass and looked out. Seeing Cao Cao's troops pressing directly beneath it, he wrote three letters in succession under cover of night, tied them to arrows, and shot them down beyond the pass. The next day he took leave of Chen Gong, then galloped to Lü Bu and said, “Sun Guan and the others at the pass all wish to surrender it. I have left Chen Gong there to hold it; you should attack at dusk and support them.”

Chen Deng went straight to Chen Gong and reported, “Cao Cao's troops have already taken a byroad into the interior of the pass. I fear Xuzhou may be lost. You and your men must hurry back.” Chen Gong therefore led his men in abandoning the pass and withdrawing. Chen Deng then lit a fire atop the pass. Lü Bu attacked under cover of darkness, and in the blackness Chen Gong's troops and Lü Bu's forces fell upon one another.

p.src: Seeing the signal fire, Cao Cao's troops charged forward as one and pressed their advantage. Sun Guan and the others scattered and fled in every direction. Lü Bu fought straight through until dawn, when at last he realized that he had been tricked; he hurried back to Xuzhou with Chen Gong. When they reached the city and called for the gate to be opened, a storm of arrows rained down from the walls. From the gate tower Mi Zhu shouted, “You seized my lord's city, and now it must be restored to him. You shall never enter this city again!” Enraged, Lü Bu cried, “Where is Chen Gui?” Mi Zhu replied, “I have already killed him.” Lü Bu turned to Chen Gong and asked, “Where is Chen Deng?” Chen Gong replied, “Can you still be so blind as to ask after that treacherous rogue?”

p.src: Lü Bu ordered a search throughout the army, but he was nowhere to be found. Chen Gong urged Lü Bu to hasten to Xiaopei, and Lü Bu followed his advice. Halfway there, they saw a troop come galloping toward them; it proved to be Gao Shun and Zhang Liao. When Lü Bu questioned them, they replied, “Chen Deng reported that our lord was surrounded, so we hurried here to rescue you.” Chen Gong said, “This too is that treacherous villain’s scheme.” Lü Bu cried angrily, “I shall surely kill that villain!” He spurred his horse and hastened to Xiaopei. But Cao Cao’s banners were flying all over the walls. Cao Cao had already ordered Cao Ren to seize the city and occupy it with his troops. From below the walls, Lü Bu bitterly cursed Chen Deng. Pointing down at Lü Bu from the wall, Chen Deng cursed him in return: “I am a servant of the Han! How could I ever serve a rebel like you?” Lü Bu flew into a rage. Just as he was about to attack the city, a great roar suddenly rose behind him and a force came charging up. The general at their head was Zhang Fei. Gao Shun rode out to meet him but could not prevail. Lü Bu himself engaged Zhang Fei. While they were fighting, cries arose once more beyond the battle lines: Cao Cao himself was leading his great army in a charge.

p.src: Realizing that he could not withstand them, Lü Bu led his army eastward. Cao Cao’s troops pursued close behind. Lü Bu fled until men and horses alike were exhausted. Suddenly a force swept out and blocked his way. At its head a general reined in his horse, held his saber crosswise, and thundered, “Lü Bu, go no farther! Guan Yunchang is here!” Lü Bu hurriedly met him in combat. Zhang Fei came racing up from behind. With no heart to prolong the fight, Lü Bu and Chen Gong fought their way through and made straight for Xiapi. Hou Cheng led out troops to receive them. When Guan Yu and Zhang Fei met, each shed tears as they recounted what had happened since their separation. Yunchang said, “I was encamped on the road to Haizhou. When I learned what had happened, I came here.” Zhang Fei said, “I have been staying at Mount Mangdang all this while. How fortunate that we should meet today!”

p.src: When the two had finished exchanging their stories, they led their forces together to see Xuande and fell weeping to the ground before him. Overcome by mingled grief and joy, Xuande took them to meet Cao Cao, then accompanied Cao into Xuzhou. Mi Zhu received him and reported in detail that his family was safe, greatly delighting Xuande. Chen Gui and his son also came to pay their respects to Cao Cao. Cao Cao held a great banquet to reward his generals. Cao Cao occupied the central seat, placing Chen Gui on his left and Xuande on his right. The other officers and soldiers took their seats according to rank. After the feast, Cao Cao commended Chen Gui and his son for their service, increased their emolument by the revenues of ten counties, and appointed Chen Deng General Who Calms the Waves.

p.src: Now Cao Cao was greatly delighted at having gained Xuzhou and discussed raising an army to attack Xiapi. Cheng Yu said, “Lü Bu now has only the single city of Xiapi. If we press him too hard, he will fight to the death and then seek refuge with Yuan Shu. If Lü Bu joins forces with Yuan Shu, their combined strength will be hard to overcome. For now, we should appoint a capable man to guard the main roads to Huainan, holding Lü Bu in check within and resisting Yuan Shu without. Moreover, Zang Ba, Sun Guan, and their followers in Shandong have not yet submitted; we must not neglect our defenses against them either.”

p.src: As for Lü Bu in Xiapi, trusting in his ample provisions and the natural defense of the Si River, he calmly settled in to hold the city, confident that nothing could go wrong. Chen Gong said, “Cao Cao’s army has only just arrived. We can strike his weary troops with our rested forces before his camp and palisades are secure; victory is certain.” Lü Bu said, “I have suffered defeat after defeat of late; we must not venture out rashly. Let them attack first, and then we shall strike; they will all fall into the Si River.” Thus he refused to heed Chen Gong’s advice.

p.src: Several days passed, and Cao Cao’s army completed its encampment. Cao Cao led his generals beneath the city walls and loudly called for Lü Bu to parley. Lü Bu appeared atop the wall. Cao Cao said to him, “I heard that Fengxian again intended to seal a marriage alliance with Yuan Shu, and so I have led my army here. Yuan Shu is guilty of the monstrous crime of rebellion, whereas you, sir, earned merit by attacking Dong Zhuo. Why now cast away your former achievement and follow a rebel? Once the city falls, repentance will come too late! If you surrender early and join me in supporting the imperial house, you shall not lose the rank of marquis.” Lü Bu replied, “Withdraw for the moment, Chancellor, and allow me time to consider.”

p.src: Standing beside Lü Bu, Chen Gong reviled Cao Cao as a treacherous villain and loosed an arrow that struck his commander’s canopy. Pointing at Chen Gong, Cao Cao cried bitterly, “I swear I will kill you!” He then led his troops in an assault on the city. Chen Gong said to Lü Bu, “Cao Cao has come from afar and cannot maintain his position for long. General, take the infantry and cavalry and establish a camp outside, while I keep the remaining troops within and hold the city fast. If Cao Cao attacks you, I shall lead troops out and strike him from the rear; if he attacks the city, you can come to its rescue from behind. Within ten days Cao Cao’s provisions will be exhausted, and we can rout him with a single charge. This is the strategy of mutually supporting horns.” Lü Bu said, “Your proposal is entirely sound.” He returned to his residence to prepare his battle gear. As it was the depths of winter, he ordered his attendants to take plenty of padded clothing.

p.src: When Lü Bu’s wife, Lady Yan, heard of this, she came out and asked, “Where are you going, my lord?” Lü Bu told her of Chen Gong’s plan. Lady Yan said, “If you entrust the whole city to others, abandon your wife and children, and lead a lone army far afield, then should some sudden change occur, how could I remain your wife?” Lü Bu hesitated, unable to decide, and did not march for three days. Chen Gong came to see him and said, “Cao Cao’s army has surrounded the city on every side. Unless we sally out soon, we are sure to be trapped.” Lü Bu said, “I have been thinking that firm defense is better than venturing far afield.” Chen Gong said, “I recently heard that Cao Cao’s army is short of provisions and has sent men to the capital, Xu, to fetch supplies. They will arrive at any time. General, take your finest troops and cut their supply route. It is an excellent plan.”

p.src: At the second watch the following night, Lü Bu wrapped his daughter’s body in silk padding, encased her in armor, strapped her to his back, took up his halberd, and mounted his horse. The city gate was opened, and Lü Bu rode out first, with Zhang Liao and Gao Shun following. As they neared Xuande’s camp, a drum thundered. Guan Yu and Zhang Fei blocked their path, shouting, “You shall not escape!” Lü Bu had no desire to prolong the fight and thought only of forcing a path through. Xuande himself led a force into the attack, and the two armies became locked in confused battle. Brave though Lü Bu was, he had a girl bound to his back and, fearing she might be hurt, dared not charge through the close encirclement. From behind, Xu Huang and Xu Chu also came charging in, while all the troops cried, “Do not let Lü Bu get away!”

p.src: Now Cao Cao had besieged the city for two months without taking it when a sudden report arrived: “Zhang Yang, governor of Henei, marched his troops to Dongshi, intending to rescue Lü Bu; but his subordinate Yang Chou killed him and meant to present his head to you, Chancellor. Yang Chou was then killed by Sui Gu, one of Zhang Yang’s trusted officers, who has instead defected to Quancheng.” On hearing the report, Cao Cao immediately dispatched Shi Huan to pursue and behead Sui Gu. He then gathered his generals and said, “Though Zhang Yang has fortunately destroyed himself, Yuan Shao threatens us from the north, while Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu trouble us in the east, and our long siege of Xiapi has yet to succeed. I wish to abandon the campaign against Lü Bu and return to the capital, suspending hostilities for the present. What say you?” Xun You hastily objected: “You must not. Lü Bu has suffered repeated defeats, and his fighting spirit has already collapsed. An army takes its commander as its heart; when the commander’s spirit fails, the soldiers lose all will to fight. Chen Gong may be resourceful, but he is slow to act. Before Lü Bu recovers his spirit and Chen Gong settles upon a plan, attack them with all speed, and Lü Bu can be captured.” Guo Jia said, “I have a plan that can break Xiapi at once and will avail us more than an army of two hundred thousand.” Xun Yu said, “Can you mean releasing the waters of the Yi and Si rivers?” Guo Jia laughed. “That is precisely my thought.”

p.src: Cao Cao was overjoyed. He immediately ordered his soldiers to breach the banks of both rivers. Cao Cao’s troops occupied the high ground and sat watching as the waters submerged Xiapi. Of all Xiapi, only the eastern gate remained beyond the floodwaters; every other gate was inundated. The soldiers hurried to report this to Lü Bu. Lü Bu said, “I have the Red Hare, which crosses water as though it were level ground. What have I to fear?” Thereafter he spent every day drinking deeply with his wives and concubines. Excessive wine and women ravaged his health, and his appearance grew wasted. One day he looked at himself in a mirror and exclaimed in alarm, “Wine and women have ruined my health! From this day onward, I must abstain.” He then issued an order that anyone in the city who drank wine would be beheaded.

Xu Huang brought Chen Gong in, freed from his bonds. What has come of it now?” Chen Gong glanced at Lü Bu and said, “My bitter regret is that this man would not heed my words! Had he followed my counsel, we might not have been captured.” Cao Cao asked, “What, then, is to be done about today's affair?” Chen Gong declared loudly, “Today there is nothing but death!” Cao Cao said, “If that is your choice, what is to become of your aged mother, your wife, and your children?” Chen Gong replied, “I have heard that one who governs the realm through filial piety does not harm another man's parents; and one who extends benevolent rule throughout the realm does not extinguish another man's line. Whether my aged mother, wife, and children live or die rests entirely with you, my enlightened lord. Now that I have been captured, I ask only to be executed at once. I have no further concern.”

u.src: Lü Bu fell silent.
Presently, the guards crowded in with Gao Shun.
Cao Cao asked, “Have you anything to say?”
Gao Shun made no reply.
Cao Cao angrily ordered his execution.
Xu Huang brought Chen Gong in, freed from his bonds.
Cao Cao said, “Gongtai, have you fared well since we parted?”
Chen Gong replied, “Your heart was corrupt, and that is why I abandoned you!”
Cao Cao said, “If my heart was corrupt, why did you choose to serve Lü Bu alone?”
Chen Gong replied, “Lü Bu may have lacked wisdom, but he was not as treacherous, deceitful, and vicious as you.”
Cao Cao said, “You considered yourself resourceful and full of stratagems. What has come of it now?”

p.src: Cao Cao felt reluctant to let him die. But Chen Gong strode straight down the tower, and the attendants could not hold him back. Cao Cao rose and tearfully saw him off. Chen Gong never once looked back. Cao Cao told his attendants, “Escort Gongtai's aged mother, wife, and children back to the capital Xu and care for them there. Anyone who neglects them shall be put to death.” Chen Gong heard this but still said nothing. He stretched out his neck and submitted to the blade. Everyone shed tears. p.src: As Cao Cao was escorting Chen Gong down from the tower, Lü Bu said to Xuande, “You are an honored guest at the table while I am a prisoner beneath the steps. Why will you not say a word to secure me some mercy?” Xuande nodded. When Cao Cao returned to the tower, Lü Bu called out, “Your greatest concern, my lord, has been none other than me. Now I have submitted. If you command as chief general and I serve as your deputy, the realm will not be difficult to pacify.” Cao Cao looked back at Xuande and asked, “What do you think?” Xuande replied, “Have you not seen what befell Ding Jianyang and Dong Zhuo?” Lü Bu glared at Xuande and said, “This fellow is the most faithless man of all!” Cao Cao ordered that Lü Bu be taken below and strangled. Lü Bu looked back at Xuande and cried, “Big-Eared Wretch! Have you forgotten when I shot the halberd at the camp gate?” Suddenly a man shouted, “Lü Bu, you common brute! If you must die, then die! What is there to fear?” They looked and saw the executioners bringing Zhang Liao forward. Cao Cao had Lü Bu strangled to death and then beheaded. A later poet lamented him in verse:

p.src: Now the guards brought Zhang Liao forward. Pointing at him, Cao Cao said, “This man looks remarkably familiar.” Zhang Liao said, “We once met inside Puyang. How can you have forgotten?” Cao Cao laughed. “So you remember too!” Zhang Liao said, “I only regret one thing!” Cao Cao asked, “What do you regret?” Zhang Liao replied, “I regret that the fire that day was not fierce enough to burn you, traitor to the realm, to death!” Cao Cao flew into a rage. “How dare a defeated general insult me!” He drew his sword and advanced to kill Zhang Liao himself. Zhang Liao showed no trace of fear, but bared his neck and waited for the stroke.
